title: larvae.toml
description: Configuration for larvae, one toolchain for all of Luau: transforms today, formatting and linting next.

extends.description: Path of a base config that this file layers over, relative to this file, ex: "./shared/larvae.base.toml". The base loads first and this file wins key by key; arrays and scalars replace whole. A base can extend another base.

exclude.description: Paths that every command skips, as globs relative to the project root, ex: ["gen/**"]. Naming a directory is enough. The include of an area wins over this list for that area, and a file named on the command line is still read.

include.description: Paths that come back in over the root `exclude`, as globs relative to the project root. This list cancels the root `exclude` and only that; the exclude of an area still applies.

input.description: Short form of `[process] input`. Source directory, or a list of them. Writing both spellings is an error.

output.description: Short form of `[process] output`. Writing both spellings is an error.

target.description: Short form of `[requires] target`. roblox-string: native @game/./@self string requires. path: relative filesystem paths (Lune). roblox-instance: Instance expressions like script.Parent:FindFirstChild("x") (see indexing_style). Writing both spellings is an error.

profile.description: Per-environment overlays selected with --profile <name>. Tables deep-merge per key; arrays and scalars are replaced whole.

aliases.description: Require aliases. Optional: .luaurc aliases work with zero config; entries here merge over them per key. Values are @game/... DataModel paths or filesystem paths. "@self" and "@game" are reserved.

additionalProperties.description: A DataModel path ("@game/ReplicatedStorage/packages") or a filesystem path ("./Packages/signal").

process.description: What to read, where to write, how to print.

input.description: Source directory, or a list of them. One root flattens into the output, several keep their own directory so two roots cannot collide.

include.description: Globs relative to the project root that pick which found files are transformed; the rest are copied.

exclude.description: Globs relative to the project root that `larvae process` skips fully: not transformed and not copied. Naming a directory is enough.

generator.description: How the output prints. retain-lines: the output keeps the lines of the input, so stack traces map. dense: the minifier, tuned by [minify]. readable: the formatter, with the [fmt] style of the project.

quotes.description: Quote style for require strings in the output. preserve keeps whatever the source used, double/single requote every require string and generated instance expression.

run_order.description: Where larvae's own rules sit in the sequence. A worm runs after this unless it says otherwise, so a worm asking to run "before" gets a smaller number and "after" a larger one.
run_order.$comment: Between two slots the buffer is spliced and re-lexed, so a later stage reads what an earlier one produced.

strip_flags.description: Drop flag comments, the `-- larvae: allow(...)` and `-- selene: allow(...)` ones, from the output. They are instructions to larvae rather than notes to a reader, so they are scaffolding the build does not need to ship. Ordinary comments are untouched. Set false when the output is read by people rather than by a game. Ignored when [rules] remove_comments is on, since that speaks for every comment already.
strip_flags.$comment: Flag comments are read by `larvae lint` to suppress a finding on the line they sit on, and the line below.

requires.description: The require-rewriting transform. Input semantics are always Luau-RFC "luau" mode.

target.description: roblox-string: native @game/./@self string requires. path: relative filesystem paths (Lune). roblox-instance: Instance expressions like script.Parent:FindFirstChild("x") (see indexing_style).

sourcemap.description: Path to a rojo sourcemap.json. Rojo's own file to instance map, which settles the cases a project file cannot describe on its own. It wins over auto mounts and is part of the cache key, so a stale one cannot produce stale requires.

mounts.description: Fallback filesystem->DataModel mapping; rarely needed with a Rojo project file. Keys are directories relative to the project root.

strict.description: Upgrade warn-level classes (missing target file, case mismatch) to errors. Unknown aliases and inexpressible/realm-violating requires are ALWAYS errors.

instance_input.description: Read require(script.Parent.Foo) style requires as input and rewrite them to the configured target. Turn it off to leave instance requires exactly as written.

client_relative_requires.description: Write a require whose two ends both sit in the StarterPlayer tree as a relative ./ or ../ path. Roblox clones a Starter container into each player, so the script that runs is a copy and a DataModel path names the template. Off by default: it lets a relative walk cross a mount boundary inside one container. A shared file that requires client code stays an error either way.

overrides.description: A different require target for the paths a glob matches, relative to [process].input. First match wins. The value is a target name, or a table with target and indexing_style.

indexing_style.description: roblox-instance target only: how emitted Instance chains index children. find_first_child -> :FindFirstChild("x"), wait_for_child -> :WaitForChild("x"), property -> .x (the dot format). Kebab-case spellings are accepted too.

rojo.description: Rojo project integration: auto-derived mounts and the derived build project in .larvae/.

build_project.description: Override the derived build project location (default: <cache_dir>/build.project.json).

defines.description: Compile-time constants, injected as globals and constant-folded. Override per profile for dev/release builds.

rule.description: false = off (default), true = on, or a table with rule options and per-rule file filters (apply_to/skip globs).

rules.description: Builtin transforms, all off by default. Every darklua rule name is accepted so configs port over 1:1. Rules that are not implemented yet error at load time naming their milestone. darklua's convert_require lives in [requires], inject_global_value in [defines], remove_spaces in the dense generator.

const_requires.description: larvae only. Turn `local X = require(...)` into `const X = require(...)`. Skips multi bindings and annotated locals. Implemented.

remove_comments.description: Remove comments. `true`, or a table with `except` regexes for comments to keep (defaults to ["^--!"] so Luau directives survive; set [] to match darklua). Implemented.

append_text_comment.description: Insert a comment at the start or end of every file. Implemented.

text.description: Literal comment text, mutually exclusive with file

file.description: Read the comment text from this file

add_luau_directive.description: larvae only. Write a Luau directive at the top of every file, ex: "strict" emits --!strict. An existing directive of the same family is left alone. Implemented.

remove_calls.description: larvae only. Remove statement position calls to the named functions, ex: print or debug.profilebegin. Names may be dotted paths; method calls and computed callees are never matched, and a call whose value is used is left alone. Implemented.

preserve_arguments_side_effects.description: Keep calls whose arguments call something, since that inner call may be the point of the line

use_get_service.description: larvae only. Rewrite `game.Players` into `game:GetService("Players")` for the known services, which keeps working when a service is renamed or not created yet. A local named game defeats it. Implemented.

dedupe_requires.description: larvae only. Top level `local X = require(...)` statements that resolve to the same module collapse, the later ones become aliases of the first. Skips const, annotated and multi binding locals. Implemented.

inject_module_path.description: larvae only. Name of a constant defined at the top of every file that references it, holding that file's DataModel path, ex: "@game/ReplicatedStorage/shared/util". Warns when no mount covers the file. Implemented.

freeze_module.description: larvae only. Wrap a module's returned table in `table.freeze`, only when nothing can write to it, so field writes, rebinds and metatable patterns turn the rule off for that file. Implemented.

compute_expression.description: Fold constant expressions to their value. Only folds when the result prints back exactly, so fractions, values past exact double range and strings holding escapes are left alone. Implemented.

convert_function_to_assignment.description: Rewrite `function foo()` into `foo = function()`, and `function o:m()` into `o.m = function(self)`. Attributed functions are left alone. Implemented.

convert_index_to_field.description: Rewrite `t["field"]` into `t.field`, and the same for table constructor keys, when the literal spells a valid name that is not a reserved word. Implemented.

convert_local_function_to_assign.description: Rewrite `local function f()` into `local f = function()`, only when the body never mentions f, since the local form is in scope inside itself. Implemented.

convert_luau_number.description: Rewrite binary literals like 0b1010 as hex and strip digit separators, both being Luau only syntax. Implemented.

convert_square_root_call.description: Rewrite `math.sqrt(x)` into `(x ^ 0.5)`. The result is always parenthesised so it survives being the base of another power. Implemented.

filter_after_early_return.description: Delete the statements after a `do ... return ... end` block, which can never run. Stops if a type alias is among them, since an exported one is visible outside the block. Implemented.

group_local_assignment.description: Merge a run of adjacent local declarations into one. Conservative, it stops at a call, a dependency between them, an annotation, a comment or anything but whitespace in between. Implemented.

make_assignment_local.description: Turn a `const` declaration back into a `local` one, the inverse of const_requires, for output that has to stay plain Lua. Implemented.

preserve_arguments_side_effects.description: Keep calls whose arguments call something, since that inner call may be the point of the line

remove_attribute.description: Strip function attributes, ex: @native. `true` removes every one, or a table with `match` regexes tested against the attribute name without its @. Implemented.

match.description: Regexes tested against the attribute name, empty means every attribute

remove_compound_assignment.description: Expand `x += 1` into `x = x + 1` for every compound operator. Targets that would have to run code twice, ex: a computed key holding a call, are left alone. Implemented.

remove_continue.description: Rewrite a loop containing `continue` into the `repeat ... until true` form with `continue` spelled `break`. Loops that also break at the same level, and repeat loops whose condition can read body locals, are left alone. Implemented.

preserve_arguments_side_effects.description: Keep calls whose arguments call something, since that inner call may be the point of the line

remove_empty_do.description: Drop `do end` blocks that contain nothing. A lone semicolon counts as content. Nested empties shed one layer per run. Implemented.

remove_floor_division.description: Rewrite `a // b` into `math.floor(a / b)`, and `a //= b` into `a = math.floor(a / b)`. Implemented.

remove_function_call_parens.description: Rewrite `f("x")` into `f"x"` and `f({})` into `f{}` when a call takes exactly one string or table argument. Implemented.

remove_if_expression.description: Rewrite `if c then a else b` into `c and a or b`. Only applied when the then value can never be false or nil, otherwise the and/or form would not be equivalent and the expression is left alone. Implemented.

remove_interpolated_string.description: Rewrite backtick strings into string.format calls. `true`, or a table with `strategy`, "string" wraps each value in tostring and formats with %s, "tostring" uses Luau's %*. Multi line and nested backtick strings are left alone. Implemented.

remove_method_call.description: Rewrite `obj:m(x)` into `obj.m(obj, x)`. Only for a plain identifier receiver, anything else would be evaluated twice. Implemented.

remove_method_definition.description: Rewrite `function C:m()` into `function C.m(self)`, making the implicit self parameter explicit. Implemented.

remove_nil_declaration.description: Rewrite `local x = nil` into `local x` and drop trailing nil values from multi bindings. Skips const, which must keep a value. Implemented.

remove_types.description: Strip every type annotation, bindings, parameters, return types, generic lists, type aliases and the tail of a `::` assertion. Implemented.

remove_unused_if_branch.description: Prune if branches whose condition is a known constant. A branch that always runs is unwrapped, or becomes a `do` block when it declares locals so their scope is preserved. Implemented.

remove_unused_variable.description: Remove unused locals and local functions.

remove_unused_while.description: Delete a while loop whose condition is a constant false. Implemented.

rename_variables.description: Rename locals and params to short names.

fmt.description:
Formatter settings for `larvae fmt`. Every stylua option under its own name, so a stylua.toml can move in here whole, plus the ones stylua does not have. A stylua.toml left in the project is still read, and these keys layer over it.

[Formatting reference →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting)

additionalProperties.description: The format options of one worm, under its key. Run `larvae self code` to name and describe them here.

block_newline_gaps.description:
Whether a blank line the author left at the very start or end of a block survives.

[block_newline_gaps →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#block-newline-gaps)

call_parentheses.description:
Whether a call with one string or table argument keeps its parentheses. "input" keeps whatever the author wrote. "as-needed" is the same setting as "none" under the name Biome and Prettier use. Both drop the parentheses only where Luau allows the bare form, which is one string or one table; a single identifier keeps them, because `h a` is a syntax error.

[call_parentheses →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#call-parentheses)

collapse_simple_statement.description:
Which one-line bodies may stay on one line.

[collapse_simple_statement →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#collapse-simple-statement)

column_width.description:
The width to fit lines into. A line only breaks when it has to.

[column_width →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#column-width)

enabled.description:
Whether `larvae fmt` changes this project at all. `false` leaves every file as it is, `--check` included, and the editor gets a formatter with no edits. This is for a project that wants larvae for its lints and its requires and keeps another formatter.

[enabled →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#enabled)

exclude.description:
Paths `larvae fmt` walks past, as globs relative to the project root, ex: ["Packages/**"]. Naming a directory is enough. A file named on the command line is still formatted, since naming it is saying you meant it.

[exclude →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#exclude)

final_newline.description:
Whether the file ends with a newline. On by default. POSIX defines a line as text up to a newline, so a file without a final one ends in something that is not a line. This covers the single trailing newline only. Larvae removes whitespace at the end of every line whatever this says.

[final_newline →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#final-newline)

function_call.description:
How the argument list of a call is laid out.

[function_call →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#function-call)

expand.description:
When the argument list is opened over several lines. "when-needed" opens it only where the line does not fit, which is what larvae has always done. "always" opens every one. "never" holds it on one line, where a value inside it can still open and the line can run past "column_width".

[function_call.expand →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#function-call-expand)

style.description:
The shape of an opened argument list. "one-per-line" gives every argument a line of its own. "hug-last" keeps the arguments on the line of the call and opens the last one, which applies where that argument is a table, a function, or a string carrying its own newlines. The arguments before it do not break, so a long list of them runs past "column_width".

[function_call.style →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#function-call-style)

indent.description:
The indent levels an opened argument takes. 0 puts it at the column of the bracket.

[function_call.indent →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#function-call-indent)

function_declaration.description:
How the parameter list of a declaration is laid out.

[function_declaration →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#function-declaration)

expand.description:
When the parameter list is opened over several lines. "when-needed" opens it only where the line does not fit, which is what larvae has always done. "always" opens every one. "never" holds it on one line, where a value inside it can still open and the line can run past "column_width".

[function_declaration.expand →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#function-declaration-expand)

indent.description:
The indent levels an opened parameter takes. 0 puts it at the column of the bracket.

[function_declaration.indent →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#function-declaration-indent)

if_expression.description:
How an "if ... then ... else ..." expression is laid out. Luau has an if expression and stylua has no option for it, so a long one runs off to the right.

[if_expression →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#if-expression)

expand.description:
When the expression is opened over several lines. "never" keeps it on one line where it fits, which is what larvae has always done. "always" opens every one. "when-large" opens one wider than "width".

[if_expression.expand →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#if-expression-expand)

width.description:
The width at which "when-large" opens an expression. It also governs a nested expression in every mode, so an if inside an if waits until it earns the room on its own.

[if_expression.width →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#if-expression-width)

style.description:
The shape of an opened expression. "block" puts the value below its keyword, in the shape of an if statement. "leading" starts the line with the keyword and takes its value: "if bar" / "then a" / "else b".

[if_expression.style →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#if-expression-style)

placement.description:
Where the "if" sits once the expression is opened. "same-line" keeps it on the line of the binding. "next-line" ends the line after "=" and starts the "if" below.

[if_expression.placement →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#if-expression-placement)

indent.description:
The indent levels between a keyword line and the value below it. 0 puts the value at the column of its keyword.

[if_expression.indent →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#if-expression-indent)

include.description:
Paths `larvae fmt` reads even when an exclude matches them, as globs relative to the project root. This list wins over the `[fmt]` exclude and over the root lists.

[include →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#include)

indent_type.description:
What one level of indentation is made of.

[indent_type →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#indent-type)

indent_width.description:
Spaces per level, and the width a tab is assumed to display as when measuring a line.

[indent_width →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#indent-width)

magic_trailing_comma.description:
A trailing comma the author left in a table means "keep this expanded", so line breaking becomes something an author decides per table rather than something width alone decides. Tables only: Luau rejects `f(a, b,)`, so a call has no trailing comma to read.

[magic_trailing_comma →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#magic-trailing-comma)

prefer_const.description:
Turns a `local` that nothing reassigns into a `const`. The same rule the `prefer_const` lint reports, with the formatter making the edit. Off by default: it rewrites a keyword, which is a bigger step than moving spaces.

[prefer_const →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#prefer-const)

mutated_tables_stay_local.description:
Keep `local` on a binding the file mutates through a field, `t.x = 1` or `table.insert(t, 1)`. Off by default, because `const` is correct there: Luau enforces it against reassignment of the name and says nothing about the value. The same choice as [lint.options.prefer_const].

[prefer_const.mutated_tables_stay_local →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#prefer-const-mutated-tables-stay-local)

quote_style.description:
Where a string literal's quotes come from. The auto pair switches when the other quote needs fewer escapes; "preserve" leaves every literal exactly as written.

[quote_style →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#quote-style)

recommended.description:
Whether larvae's own defaults apply, or only the options this project wrote. Absent and `true` both mean the defaults apply. `false` starts from a base that changes as little as possible: `magic_trailing_comma`, `space_inside_braces` and `trailing_comma` go off, and the project turns back on what it wants. Every other default is either stylua's or a setting that does nothing until a project asks for it, so `false` does not move it. A `stylua.toml` states the style of the project already, so it is the base wherever one exists.

[recommended →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#recommended)

require_binding.description:
Selects which keyword binds a required module. Luau enforces "const", so a name that the file reassigns keeps "local" and does not become a syntax error. "preserve" keeps each declaration as written.

[require_binding →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#require-binding)

semicolons.description:
Whether a statement ends with a semicolon. Luau requires one only before a statement opening with "(", and larvae emits that one whatever this says. "never" and "as-needed" therefore name the same output; both are accepted.

[semicolons →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#semicolons)

sort_requires.description:
Sort the run of requires at the top of a file.

[sort_requires →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#sort-requires)

grouping.description:
"flat" is one sorted run, which is what stylua does. "by-kind" puts aliases, then absolute, then relative, with a blank line between each.

[sort_requires.grouping →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#sort-requires-grouping)

space_after_function_names.description:
Where a space goes between a function name and its parentheses.

[space_after_function_names →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#space-after-function-names)

space_inside_braces.description:
`{ a }` rather than `{a}`, which is the Luau convention.

[space_inside_braces →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#space-inside-braces)

syntax.description:
Accepted from stylua and ignored. larvae formats Luau and only Luau, which is what every value of this asks for here.

[syntax →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#syntax)

table_types.description:
How a table type is laid out, in every position a type takes: an alias, an annotation, a parameter, a return type, and a :: assertion. A table wider than "width" opens with one field per line.

[table_types →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#table-types)

enabled.description:
Off keeps the one-line replay, byte for byte what larvae wrote before.

[table_types.enabled →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#table-types-enabled)

width.description:
The width at which a table type opens over several lines. The measure is the flat form of one table alone, so a short table nested in a long one keeps its line.

[table_types.width →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#table-types-width)

separator.description:
The separator between fields, in both layouts. Luau reads both.

[table_types.separator →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#table-types-separator)

sort_table_types.description:
Sorts the properties of a table type by the length of their names, in a type position only. A value table keeps the order the author wrote. A table type that holds a comment stays as written, because a token replay has no position to put a comment back, and a sort reads the fields the table type layout finds, so table_types.enabled = false leaves every order alone.

[sort_table_types →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#sort-table-types)

order.description:
The order of the properties. "none" keeps the order the author wrote, which is the default: a formatter that reorders code nobody asked it to reorder loses the order the author chose. "ascending" puts the shortest name first and "descending" the longest. Two names of one length sort alphabetically, so the output does not depend on the order of the input.

[sort_table_types.order →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#sort-table-types-order)

indexer_first.description: The older spelling of indexer, kept so a config written for it still means what it meant: true is first and false is sorted. See https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#sort-table-types-indexer-first

indexer.description: Where an indexer such as [number]: any lands when the sort runs. first reads it as the heading of the table, last as the footnote, and sorted gives it no special place. See https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#sort-table-types-indexer

type_operators.description:
How a union and an intersection are laid out, in every position a type takes. One option covers | and &, because they share one shape: members with an operator between them.

[type_operators →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#type-operators)

expand.description:
When the chain is opened over several lines. "auto" leaves it to the replay, which is the layout larvae always had, so a chain wider than "column_width" runs past it. "always" puts every member on a line of its own, with the operator leading the line. "never" holds one line whatever table_types.width says about a table inside it, and opens one member per line only where the line passes "column_width": the order is column_width first, then type_operators, then table_types.width.

[type_operators.expand →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#type-operators-expand)

trailing_comma.description:
A table that broke over several lines keeps a trailing comma on its last field.

[trailing_comma →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#trailing-comma)

unused_imports.description:
What to do with a required module that nothing uses. "ignore" leaves it as written. "underscore" renames it to `_Name`, which keeps the module and silences the lint. "remove" deletes the declaration.

The default is "ignore" for a reason worth knowing: `require` runs a module the first time a file asks for it, so a module can do its work by being required at all, and deleting the line stops that work while the file still compiles. A name that only a type reads counts as used, so `const jecs = require("@pkg/jecs")` with `type C = jecs.Component` below it survives both modes. A name that already opens with `_` is left alone, and a statement inside a `fmt off` region is never removed.

[unused_imports →](https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#unused-imports)

order.description: Sorts the fields of a value table. Off by default: a value table is data, and the sort moves each value with its key. A table with a comment, a positional field, or a computed key that is not a plain string stays as written. See https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#sort-tables-order

sort_tables.description: How the formatter orders the fields of a value table. See https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#sort-tables

function_style.description: The keyword a top-level function declaration takes. A dotted or method name has no local form and stays as written, an anonymous function declares nothing, and const applies only where nothing reassigns the name. See https://larvae-luau.github.io/docs/reference/formatting#function-style

lint.description: Linter settings for `larvae lint`. A selene.toml left in the project is still read, and these keys layer over it. selene's own names work here too, so its file can move in whole.

not.description: options and config are two names for one table, so only one of them can be written.

enabled.description: Whether `larvae lint` reports on this project at all. `false` reports nothing, exits zero, and clears the diagnostics in the editor. This is for a project that wants larvae for its formatter and its requires and keeps another linter.

recommended.description: Whether a lint larvae recommends is on without this project saying so. Absent and `true` both mean the default levels apply. `false` starts every lint at `allow`, so the project gets the lints it names under `[lint.rules]` and no others. A level the project wrote always wins in either state.

std.description: Which globals exist before a file runs. Anything else is undefined_variable.

anyOf.description: A selene std name is accepted too: lua51, lua52, lua53, lua54 and luajit all mean "luau", and a chain like "roblox+testez" is decided by its first name.

globals.description: Extra names the project defines beyond the standard library, ex: ["shared", "_TESTING"].

exclude.description: Paths `larvae lint` walks past, as globs relative to the project root, ex: ["Packages/**"]. Naming a directory is enough. Same key selene has, and a selene.toml's list is picked up too. A file named on the command line is still linted, since naming it is saying you meant it.

include.description: Paths `larvae lint` reads even when an exclude matches them, as globs relative to the project root. This list wins over the `[lint]` exclude and over the root lists.

config.description: selene's name for [lint.options], accepted so a selene.toml can be pasted in. It is the same table, so write one or the other, not both.

lint_level.description: "allow" is off. "info" and "warn" are both reported and both leave the exit code alone; they differ in what they ask of the reader, and an editor draws an info as a hint and a warning as a squiggle. "deny" is reported and fails the run.

lint_rules.description: How loudly each lint speaks. A lint keeps its own default until it is named here. A name not listed below is a worm's lint, declared in that worm's [lints] and levelled here the same way.

additionalProperties.description: The lints of one worm, under its key. Run `larvae self code` to name and describe them here.

almost_swapped.description: Two assignments that look like a swap but overwrite one of the values. Default: warn.

and_or_conditional.description: `cond and a or b` used as a value. The decision hides inside an expression, where an if statement states one case per branch. Off by default: the form is ordinary Lua and it is correct for every truthy middle. Default: allow.

bad_comment_directive.description: A --! directive that Luau does not know, or one that comes after the code it should govern. Default: warn.

bad_string_escape.description: An escape sequence the language does not define. Default: warn.

builtin_global_write.description: An assignment over a standard global, which every later script sees. Default: warn.

builtin_shadowed.description: A local that takes the name of a standard global, such as `local table = {}`. The library is unreachable for the rest of the scope, and the failure lands at the first line that wanted it. Default: warn.

collapsible_if.description: An if that holds one if and nothing else. The two conditions are one `and` apart, and the nesting says they are not. Default: allow.

compare_nan.description: Comparing against nan, which is never equal to anything including itself. Default: warn.

comparison_precedence.description: not a == b, or a chain like a < b < c, which does not group the way it reads. Default: warn.

constant_condition.description: A condition that is a literal, so the branch is decided before the program runs. Only nil and false are false in Luau, so `if 0 then` and `if "" then` both pass. `while true do` and `repeat ... until false` are exempt, because both are standard loops. Default: warn.

constant_table_comparison.description: Comparing against a table literal, which compares identity and is always false. Default: warn.

deprecated.description: A function that still works but has been replaced. Default: warn. Extend it under [lint.options.deprecated].

divide_by_zero.description: Dividing by a literal zero. Default: warn.

duplicate_function.description: Two functions of the same name in one scope, where the first is discarded. Default: warn.

duplicate_keys.description: A table key written twice, where only the last one survives. Default: warn.

duplicate_local.description: One local statement or parameter list that declares the same name twice. Default: warn.

else_after_return.description: An else after a branch that returns, breaks or continues. The else costs a level of indent and buys nothing. Every branch must end in the jump, because an elseif that falls through still needs the else. Default: allow.

empty_if.description: An if branch with nothing in it. Default: warn.

empty_loop.description: A loop body with nothing in it. Default: warn.

format_string.description: A format string that string.format or os.date rejects at runtime. Default: warn.

global_usage.description: Reaching into _G, which is shared with every other script. Default: warn.

high_cyclomatic_complexity.description: A function with more branches than anyone can hold at once. Default: allow. Threshold under [lint.options.high_cyclomatic_complexity].

if_expression_assignment.description: `if cond then a else b` used as a value. Off by default, and it has to stay off: misleading_and_or names this exact form as the repair, so a default that reported would report the fix larvae asked for. Default: allow.

if_same_then_else.description: Two branches of the same if with identical bodies. Default: warn.

ifs_same_cond.description: An elseif repeating a condition already tested, which can never run. Default: warn.

ignored_pcall_result.description: A pcall or xpcall used as a statement. It catches the error and discards it, so the failure leaves no trace at all. Default: warn.

implicit_any_local.description: A local declared with no value and no type, so what it holds is decided by whatever assigns it first. In a file with no `--!strict` directive Luau accepts any later assignment of any type, which is the implicit `any` this names. A local that nothing ever assigns is left to `uninitialized_local`, which says the more urgent thing about the same line. The only lint larvae denies by default, because the fix is an annotation and an annotation changes no behaviour. Default: deny.

implicit_any_parameter.description: A parameter with no type, so what the function takes is decided by each caller. The sibling of implicit_any_local, on the other side of the call. Off by default: most Luau carries no annotations, so a warn default would report hundreds of times on the first run. Default: allow.

implicit_return.description: A function that returns a value on one path and falls off the end on another. The lint is off by default, because a lookup that returns nil when it finds nothing is idiomatic Luau. Default: warn.

length_as_condition.description: #t used as a condition. A length is a number and every number is true in Luau, so the guard does nothing and the branch runs every time. Default: deny.

loop_invariant_call.description: A call inside a loop whose result cannot change between iterations. Default: warn.

manual_table_clone.description: A loop that copies a table, which table.clone does in one call. Default: warn.

misleading_and_or.description: cond and false or b, which always gives b because the middle is never truthy. Default: warn.

mismatched_arg_count.description: Calling a function in this file with the wrong number of arguments. Default: warn.

mixed_table.description: A table with both array entries and named keys. Default: warn.

multiple_statements.description: More than one statement on a line. Default: warn.

must_use.description: Calling a pure function and discarding what it returned. Default: warn.

negated_condition.description: An if with a negated condition and an else. Dropping the not and swapping the bodies states the same thing in the order a reader expects. Default: allow.

non_const_require.description: A required module bound with local, where const says it never changes. The lint skips a name that the file reassigns, because const would then be a syntax error. Default: allow.

number_literal_overflow.description: A hexadecimal or binary literal wider than 64 bits, which is truncated. Default: warn.

parenthese_conditions.description: Parentheses around a condition, which Luau does not need. Default: warn.

placeholder_read.description: Reading _, the name that says a value is discarded. Default: warn.

prefer_const.description: A local that nothing reassigns, which `const` states outright. Off by default: `const` is larvae's own reading of Luau and not every project writes it, so a codebase of ordinary `local` would report on nearly every line the first time it ran. Tune it under [lint.options.prefer_const]. Default: allow.

restricted_globals.description: Reading a global the project has ruled out. Silent until the project fills in [lint.options.restricted_globals], so the default level costs nothing. Each entry is a name and the reason a reader is shown. Default: warn.

restricted_module_paths.description: Requiring a module the project has ruled out. Default: warn, and quiet until [lint.options.restricted_module_paths] names something.

roblox_incorrect_color3_new_bounds.description: Color3.new given a channel over 1, where the scale is 0 to 1. Default: warn.

roblox_manual_fromscale_or_fromoffset.description: A UDim2.new that fromScale or fromOffset says more clearly. Default: warn.

roblox_suspicious_udim2_new.description: UDim2.new given two arguments, where it takes four. Default: warn.

self_assignment.description: Assigning a value to itself, which does nothing. Default: warn.

shadowing.description: A name that hides another still in scope. Default: warn.

string_concat_in_loop.description: Building a string by concatenation in a loop, which is quadratic. Default: warn.

suspicious_reverse_loop.description: A numeric for counting down without a negative step, which never runs. Default: warn.

table_operations.description: A table.insert or table.remove whose index or argument count is wrong. Default: warn.

type_check_inside_call.description: A comparison inside type(), where it belongs outside. Default: warn.

unbalanced_assignments.description: More names than values, or more values than names. Default: warn.

undefined_variable.description: A name nothing declares, which is nil at runtime. Default: deny.

uninitialized_local.description: A local declared with no value and never assigned, so every read is nil. Default: warn.

unknown_type.description: Comparing type(x) against a string that type() never returns. Default: warn.

unreachable_code.description: Statements after a return, break or continue, which never run. Default: warn.

unscoped_variables.description: An assignment with no local, which creates a global. Default: warn.

unused_function.description: A `local function` that nothing calls. The Luau compiler separates this from an unused variable and separates it by the declaring form, so `local f = function() end` is `unused_variable` and `local function f() end` is this. Both read [lint.options.unused_variable]. Default: warn.

unused_import.description: A module required and never used. Split from unused_variable: the fix is to delete the line. Reads [lint.options.unused_variable]. Default: warn.

unused_variable.description: A name declared and never read. Default: warn. Tunable under [lint.options.unused_variable].

zero_step_loop.description: A numeric for whose step is zero, so the counter never moves. Default: warn.

lint_options.description: Per-lint settings, keyed by the lint's name and handed to the lint that asked for them.

additional.description: Names the project has deprecated of its own, as old = "what to use instead".

maximum_complexity.description: Branches a function may have before it is reported. selene's default, kept so a project moving over gets the same answers.

mutated_tables_stay_local.description: Keep `local` on a binding the file mutates through a field, such as `t.x = 1` or `table.insert(t, 1)`. Off by default, because `const` is correct there: Luau enforces it against reassignment of the name and says nothing about the value, so `const t = {}` then `t.x = 1` compiles. Turn it on where `local` is read as "this one changes".

restricted_globals.description: Globals this project rules out, as `name = "why"`. The reason is the message a reader gets, so a bare list of names would report "this is restricted" and leave them guessing.

paths.description: Require paths the project forbids, as path = "why".

parameters.description: Report unused function parameters too. Off by default: a parameter is part of a signature the caller decides.

loop_variables.description: Report unused `for` variables too. Off by default: `for k, v` where only `k` is wanted is how the language is written.

ignore_pattern.description: Names exempted, as a regular expression.

worm_config.description: This worm's own settings, handed to it untouched at init. larvae never reads inside one, so whatever the worm documents goes here. A table of its own, so a key the worm calls `repo` cannot collide with the one saying where to fetch it from.

worms.description: Worms, extensions loaded from a GitHub release. A worm is Luau source or a wasm32 module in a zip carrying a worm.toml. The key names the worm and has to match `name` in its worm.toml, since it is also what namespaces the worm's rules and its settings. (M3)

additionalProperties.description: Where the worm comes from, plus anything the project wants to say about it. Name repo and version, or path, never both.

version.description: Which release to install. "^" takes the newest on every install, which is what `larvae worm add` writes. A number such as "0.1.0" holds that one release and never moves. A range such as "^0.1.0" follows the newest release semver calls compatible. A leading v is accepted and dropped.

asset.description: Release asset to fetch. Defaults to <key>-worm.zip, then worm.zip. Means nothing with path, which is not a release.

path.description: A directory on disk instead of a release. Not how a worm ships, but how its author runs it before publishing.

run_order.description: Where this worm's rules sit relative to larvae's own. "before" means larvae's rules see this worm's output. An explicit slot number wins over both this and what the worm declared.

rules.description: Which of this worm's rules are on, by name. They live under the worm rather than in [rules] so a worm declaring const_requires cannot shadow the builtin.

inherit_lints.description: Run the lints of larvae on the files this worm claims. It overrides what the worm declared in its worm.toml.

inherit.description: Which inherited lints and format options apply inside the files of this worm. Inheritance takes everything unless this table states less.

lints_only.description: The only lints of larvae that run in the files of this worm.

lints_except.description: The lints of larvae that do not run in the files of this worm.

fmt_except.description: The format options that do not apply in the files of this worm. An option named here keeps its own default there.

cargo.description: A crate on crates.io that ships the worm as its binary, ex: "luaux-worm@0.1.0". cargo install builds it from source on this machine, so one crate serves every platform. Excludes repo, path, and asset; the version can sit here after @ or in the version key.

bundle.description: Single-file output for `larvae bundle`. Each module initialises on first require, so the bundle keeps the demand order of the unbundled project.

entry.description: The module the bundle starts from, relative to the project root. `--entry` overrides it.

output.description: Where the single file goes, relative to the project root. Default: bundle.luau.

tree_shake.description: Drop the modules that the entry cannot reach. Turn off to keep modules that only a dynamic require reaches.

module_ids.description: What the registry calls each module. `paths` reads well in errors and ships the project layout. `opaque` numbers the modules, so the bundle names no file and no package.

minify.description: Tuning for `generator = "dense"`. Inert under another generator.

column_span.description: The column where the dense emitter breaks the line. Line numbers in crash reports stay meaningful this way. A token wider than the span stays whole. Written here, this number also beats the unlimited span that obfuscate implies.

rename_variables.description: Give every local a short name while minifying. The same rule as [rules] rename_variables, turned on for dense builds only.

obfuscate.description: Make the output hard to read: the dense emitter whatever generator says, no types, every local named _0x0 upward, and every string literal as the \xNN form of its own bytes. The file lands on one line unless column_span says otherwise. Roblox has no loadstring, so this is what obfuscation can be: the file still has to be Luau the compiler reads.

check.description: Whole-project analyses that `larvae check` runs over the require graph. Each check is a level, like [lint.rules], so the project decides what fails CI.

cycles.description: Modules that require each other, directly or through a chain. The report names the whole cycle. Default: warn.

unused_modules.description: Modules that nothing requires. A Script or LocalScript is never reported, because Roblox runs those. Default: allow.

early_require.description: Client scripts that require through an indexing style that does not wait for replication. Only the roblox-instance target. Default: warn.

entries.description: Extra entry points, as paths relative to the project root. A module in this list is never reported as unused.

lsp.description: How `larvae lsp`, the editor server, behaves.

additionalProperties.description: The editor settings of one worm, by its name: [lsp.oop] holds the settings the oop worm declares under [options] in its manifest. The server checks every key against that declaration.

enabled.description: Off answers every request with nothing, so another server owns the files.

claim_only.description: On serves only the files that a worm claims, so stock luau-lsp can own the plain Luau. Off serves every Luau file, which is what larvae always did.

analyzer.description: Off serves what larvae always served and nothing the analyzer adds: lints, format, code actions, and the outline stay, on claimed and plain files alike, while hover, completion, and type diagnostics go quiet and the session is never built.

character_type.description: What Player.Character types to. r15 and r6 carry the body parts of their rig, so player.Character.Humanoid resolves with no cast. not_set types it as the union of the two, for a place that allows both.

sourcemap.description: The rojo sourcemap to read, relative to the root of the project. It gives every script the type of its own instance, so script.Parent and its neighbours resolve. A project without the file gets no instance tree and no message.

sourcemap_autogenerate.description: The server runs the sourcemap command itself, so the map follows every file the project adds or moves. With no command set, rojo is inferred from its project file; a generator that does not start is said once and costs the autogeneration alone.

rojo_project_file.description: The rojo project the inferred sourcemap command reads, relative to the root of the project.

sourcemap_command.description: The command that generates the sourcemap, run through the shell in the project root. Empty infers rojo: with a rojo project file in the root, larvae runs rojo sourcemap --watch; without one, nothing runs. A project on another sync tool names its own generator here, ideally one that watches.

definitions.description: Extra type definition files, loaded into the analyzer after the platform globals. Paths are relative to the root of the project. larvae analyze --definitions adds to this list.

lint_groups.description: A level for a whole kind of lint. It sits between `recommended` and [lint.rules]: a name in [lint.rules] always wins, and a group covers every lint the project did not name. Groups live here and not inside [lint.rules], because a table there already means the lints of a worm of that name.

correctness.description: The code cannot do what it says: it throws, it hangs, or a line of it is dead. Every lint of this kind that [lint.rules] does not name takes this level.

suspicious.description: Probably wrong, and a human decides. Every lint of this kind that [lint.rules] does not name takes this level.

style.description: A matter of how the code reads. Every lint of this kind that [lint.rules] does not name takes this level.

complexity.description: More shape than the job needs. Every lint of this kind that [lint.rules] does not name takes this level.

performance.description: Correct, and it costs more than it has to. Every lint of this kind that [lint.rules] does not name takes this level.

roblox.description: A Roblox data type used in a way that does not hold. Every lint of this kind that [lint.rules] does not name takes this level.

lsp_imports.description: `[lsp.completion.imports]`, the auto-import settings. The names mirror luau-lsp's `completion.imports.*`, so a user moving between the two servers keeps the setting they know. The editor extension exposes the same ids under `larvae-lsp.`; where both speak, this file wins.

enabled.description: Offer a service or module the file has not imported yet, with the binding inserted above the first statement.

require_style.description: How a module auto-import spells its require. `auto` writes an alias where one covers the module and the relative form elsewhere; `always_absolute` writes the `@game` path; `nearest_absolute` takes the shortest stable anchor: an alias, then `@game`, then relative. Default: auto.

use_const.description:
Whether an auto-import writes `const` or `local`. On by default, which departs from luau-lsp on purpose: that server defaults it off because Luau had no `const` when the setting was written, and larvae's platform has the keyword. An auto-import binds a service and nothing reassigns it, which is the clearest case for it. Off writes `local` instead.

This setting is its own thing and does not read `[fmt] require_binding`, because that option governs a `require` binding and a `game:GetService` line is not one.

enabled.description: Off answers every completion request with an empty list, so another server owns the list.

hide_deprecated.description: Drop deprecated entries from the completion list whole. Off, they stay listed with a strikethrough. Default: off.

show_keywords.description: Offer the keywords that fit the position, beside the names.

lsp_inlay_hints.description: `[lsp.inlay_hints]`, mirroring luau-lsp's `inlayHints.*`. Every one is off by default: a hint is text the editor draws into a line the author did not write, and a reader who did not ask for it reads that as the file changing under them.

variable_types.description: Draw the inferred type of a local the author left unannotated.

parameter_types.description: Draw the inferred type of a parameter the author left unannotated.

function_return_types.description: Show the inferred return type of a function, after its parameter list. Default: off.

parameter_names.description: Show the name of each parameter before the argument that fills it: on no call, on literal arguments, or on every one. An argument spelled like its parameter stays bare. Default: none.

update_delay.description: How long the hints hold still while the author types, in milliseconds. A request mid-edit answers with the last settled hints, and one refresh follows the pause. 0 recomputes on every request. Default: 700.

type_hint_max_length.description: How long a hint can be before it is cut. A hint longer than the code it annotates hides the code. luau-lsp uses 50.

lsp_signature_help.description: `[lsp.signature_help]`, mirroring luau-lsp's `signatureHelp.*`. Needs a binary built with the analyzer, because the signature comes from the type of the callee.

enabled.description: Show the signature of the call the caret sits in, with the active parameter marked.
Answer a hover with the type under the cursor.

show_table_kinds.description: Keep the `{| |}` markers that say a table is sealed. Off, as luau-lsp has it: the marker answers a question somebody writing a type asks, and a reader hovering a value is not asking it.

lsp_index.description: `[lsp.index]`, mirroring luau-lsp's `index.*`. The index reads and parses every Luau file the project holds, which measured 25ms over 300 files. A project that feels it turns the index off and keeps `documentSymbol` for the file in front of it.

enabled.description: Build the project wide symbol index that `workspace/symbol` searches.

lsp_studio.description: `[lsp.studio]`, the link to the Roblox Studio plugin. The plugin mirrors the live DataModel into larvae, so the type checker knows the instances the place actually holds and not only the ones a sourcemap describes.

enabled.description: Open the listener the plugin posts to. Off by default, and the default is a decision rather than caution: turning it on opens a listening socket, and a tool that opens one without being asked has changed what it is. The socket binds to loopback and nothing else, so the tree never leaves the machine, but any process on that machine can still reach it.

port.description: The port the plugin posts to. The plugin ships with the same number.

lsp_fflags.description: `[lsp.fflags]`, Luau's own feature flags. Luau ships a change behind a flag long before the flag flips, so a server that reads only the defaults reads an older Luau than the one it links. They apply in order: every flag on, then this table's overrides, then the two values larvae cannot work without, so a later step wins.

enable_by_default.description: Turn on every Luau analysis flag that Luau does not mark experimental. luau-lsp defaults this on; larvae defaults it off, because larvae ships one pinned Luau and the same binary to everyone, so a flag that misbehaves misbehaves for every user at once.

enable_new_solver.description: Turn on Luau's new type solver.

over.description: One value per flag name, which wins over the two switches above. The value is text because Luau keeps a boolean list and an integer list, and the name decides which one is asked: "true" and "120" are both written the same way. The editor spells this `override`, which is a Rust keyword.

lsp_bytecode.description: `[lsp.bytecode]`, how the analyzer would compile. Nothing reads these yet. They are here because the editor extension sends them, and a setting the server drops is worse than one it stores: the user changes it, nothing happens, and nothing says why.

type_info_level.description: 0 none, 1 the types the compiler knows.

vector_lib.description: The library a vector literal comes from, for a project with its own.
